analytical_proofs.primitive_domains: Positive sphere radius, tetrahedron scale, cone radius and height; optional supplied rotations in SO(3). Sphere f=|q|-R is exact signed distance. Pyramid f=max_i(-w_i.q-L)/sqrt(3) imports conv{L*w_i}; cone f=max(-z,z-H,(hypot(x,y)+(R/H)z-R)/sqrt(1+(R/H)^2)) imports its finite cone. The latter two are membership fields; exact distance is obtained from their region.
analytical_proofs.klein_formula: q=cos(u/2)sin(v)-sin(u/2)sin(2v); z=sin(u/2)sin(v)+cos(u/2)sin(2v); iota=c+ell*((a+q)cos(u),(a+q)sin(u),z). a>2, ell>0. v~v+2pi and (u+2pi,v)~(u,-v).
analytical_proofs.klein_immersion: The radial factor a+q>a-2>0. iota_u has angular component ell*(a+q), while iota_v lies in the radial/vertical plane and has norm ell*sqrt(cos(v)^2+4cos(2v)^2)>=ell*sqrt(31)/8>0. Thus iota_u and iota_v are independent everywhere on the quotient. Self-intersections of the image do not invalidate immersion and are not claimed to be an embedding.
analytical_proofs.klein_distance: The image S of the compact quotient is compact. D(x)=min_{u,v in [0,2pi]}|x-iota(u,v)| exists globally. For epsilon>0, A_epsilon={D<=epsilon}=cl{D<epsilon} is regular closed; f_epsilon=D-epsilon is a 1-Lipschitz membership field. Its canonical signed distance is d_A, generally not D-epsilon inside overlaps.
analytical_proofs.sample_bound: Set Lu=ell*sqrt((a+sqrt(2))^2+1/2), Lv=ell*sqrt(5). They uniformly bound |iota_u| and |iota_v|. A rectangular M by N periodic grid, with twisted u-edge gluing, has an image point within delta=Lu*pi/M+Lv*pi/N of every image point. Therefore 0<=D_grid(x)-D(x)<=delta for every x. This is a uniform metric error bound, not a finite-sample topology proof.
analytical_proofs.mask_lookup: For x!=0 use u=y/|x| and psi=atan2(z,x) mod 2pi, with psi=0 at both poles. For x=0 use canonical direction e_y. Alternate u in [-1,1] and psi in [0,2pi) bisections for d steps, assigning every split equality to the upper child; j_d is the resulting binary-word integer. Given finite symmetric zero-diagonal Q in F2^(N by N), set i=j_d mod N, j=(i+1+(n mod N)) mod N, M=(-1)^Q and m_n(x)=M_ij. The operation uses the pre-update Q and integer tick snapshot.
analytical_proofs.mask_seams: For fixed depth and tick the mask is constant on finite direction cells. Its seams are dyadic constant-u conical surfaces and longitude half-planes, with codimension-two intersections and the origin as exceptional representatives. On open cells the weak derivative of m*f_K is m*grad(f_K). Across an oriented smooth seam it has jump measure (m_plus-m_minus)*f_K*n_S*H^2|S; use the locally BV product rule for the Lipschitz f_K=D_K-epsilon (or its sampled-distance approximation). No Clarke gradient is claimed at a discontinuous jump. The origin/pole ownership values alone add no three-dimensional distributional atom. Import the final raw field region before canonical exact CSG; raw negation is not presumed to respect arbitrary-field Boolean laws.
analytical_proofs.analog_domain: 0<rlo<r<rhi; rstar,r0,Rs,ell,p_shark,p_Len,b,alpha>0; rc>=ell; |eps|<1; |gamma|<1; |a_phase|<1; theta in R; k!=0; |zeta|<B<pi|k|. Triangular profile c_p(x)=abs((x mod p)-p/2)-p/4 is continuous, 1-Lipschitz, piecewise slopes +/-1.
analytical_proofs.analog_stages: x=ln(r/rstar); s0=x+eps*c_p(x); rS=rstar*exp(s0); g=rc+ell*tanh((rS-rc)/ell); rg=r0*exp(alpha*(g-rc)); s=(ln(rg)-ln(rg(rlo)))/(ln(rg(rhi))-ln(rg(rlo))); t=frac(theta/(2pi)); lambda=(1-s,s*(1-t),s*t); Len=s+gamma*c_pLen(s); Theta=theta+a_phase*sin(theta-beta)*sin(2pi*Len); R=Rs*exp(b*Len); F=(R*cos(Theta),R*sin(Theta),zeta+k*Theta).
analytical_proofs.analog_monotonicity: x+eps*c_p(x) is strictly increasing: differences >=(1-|eps|)*(x2-x1). Exponential, chamber, eruption and log normalization preserve strict monotonicity. Len differences >=(1-|gamma|)*(s2-s1). R is strictly increasing in r. Theta_theta>=1-|a_phase|>0 and Theta-theta is bounded, so Theta is an onto increasing map of R for each fixed r.
analytical_proofs.analog_inverse: Recover R=hypot(X,Y), Len=ln(R/Rs)/b, then invert the increasing Len map, undo log normalization, eruption, chamber by atanh, and increasing Shark map. From principal phi=atan2(Y,X), n=nearest_integer((Z-k*phi)/(2pi*k)) is unique because |zeta|/(2pi|k|)<1/2. Theta=phi+2pi*n; invert its increasing phase map and set zeta=Z-k*Theta. Barycentric inversion gives s=lambda2+lambda3 and t=lambda3/s; retain theta turn for a flat barycentric view alone.
analytical_proofs.jacobian: On every open differentiability cell of the Shark and Len profiles, det DF=R*R_r*Theta_theta>0. At triangular corners the ordinary classical Jacobian need not exist (zero gains can remove corners); the continuous map remains strictly monotone and is a piecewise C1 homeomorphism onto its image. The determinant is positive almost everywhere. This is a parameter-coordinate determinant. For the reference helical body chi0=(r*cos(theta),r*sin(theta),zeta+k*theta), det Dchi0=r and the physical deformation gradient is DF*(Dchi0)^(-1), giving physical volume ratio J=R*R_r*Theta_theta/r>0 a.e.
analytical_proofs.injectivity: Equal Cartesian outputs give equal R and hence r. Equal planar phases give Theta1-Theta2=2pi*n. Equal Z implies zeta1-zeta2=-2pi*k*n. Since |zeta1-zeta2|<2B<2pi|k|, n=0; strict phase monotonicity gives theta1=theta2 and then zeta1=zeta2. Without the thickness bound, distinct turns can overlap in 3D.
analytical_proofs.feedback: P contains explicit sphere/cone/pyramid union data. q_n=1[f_Pn(p_sample)<=0]; b_next=b_n XOR q_n; stored sphere radius R_next=1+(1/4)b_next. Inputs are read before next state is written. Positive radii follow directly for binary b. Entity ID and payload are copied unchanged; geometry evaluation actually changes the stored next program. This is one concrete self-referential specialization, not a claim of universal autopoiesis.
